architecture_findings: Win3x menu_scope.c and Win2000 system_menu.c each own TLS stack/thread hook/callback retirement; moving files alone would preserve separate engines

Product common engine should follow existing shared runtime ownership pattern; importing USER32/COMCTL32 into ntwshk would break its console-safe import invariant, so any GUI binding must remain lazy outside loader-lock
Renderer remains responsible for actual drawing/support/geometry; public engine must own scope/popup identity, hooks, reentry and cleanup; final API awaits complete finite review
Win3x menu_bar and iteration use field-pointer views/private style_window; S8 replaces actual owner/tracking state, not just files or wrappers
Win3x tracking uses WH_GETMESSAGE PM_REMOVE; Win2000 uses WH_MSGFILTER MSGF_MENU; shared engine must preserve this existing backend difference as explicit mode, not silently merge message semantics
Menu dispatch fixture unconditionally created a private desktop; removed that entry before any native execution. Other isolated_process users must be invoked with --private-worker

migration_batches.owns: one shared per-thread scope/observer stack, popup/shadow identities, callback refs, detached retirement and observer hook lifetime
